title: Eval regression: contextual alert routing, rate‑limit and noise reduction for Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Reduce alert noise while preserving timely detection of quality regressions caused by config or model changes. Deliver a Console-first feature that: 1) automatically correlates eval regression signals with recent model/config deltas; 2) routes alerts with contextual snapshots to the right channel (Slack channel per team, PagerDuty for SEV/production SLO breaches); 3) applies smart rate‑limits and grouping to avoid duped/unanalyzable fires.

Scope: backend correlation service + Console UI timeline and routing config + integrations for Slack and PagerDuty + rate‑limit/grouping logic + audit/logging for postmortems. Excludes building new eval metrics themselves (we consume existing eval pipelines), but includes a small controlled rerun mechanism for immediate context gather on config change.

Success metrics: reduce duplicate PagerDuty incidents by >=60% in first 30 days, reduce Slack alert volume by >=50% for teams with heavy eval churn, maintain median time‑to-action <= 15m for high confidence regressions.

Deliverables: PRD, interaction spec (Console timeline view), routing policy UI, backend correlation job, Slack message templates, PagerDuty incident enrichment, runbook for SEV handling, migration guide for teams to opt into contextual routing.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: Product, Eng (runtime + platform), Design, and SRE met. Agreed to prioritize correlation by CLUSTER of change (model version, quantization profile, batching config) rather than individual diff hunks to keep signal stable.

2026-02-25 - Eng scoping (Samir Gupta): initial approach is an async correlation pipeline that watches config commits and eval ingestion. We will store a short-lived context snapshot (prompt set, seed subset, model checksum) for fast reruns. Concern: snapshot storage could increase costs; proposed TTL 14 days and compression of artifacts.

2026-02-28 - Design feedback (Priya Rao): Console timeline should visually pin the config diff above the eval trend and include a one‑click "rerun sample" modal that returns tokenized diff and changed outputs. Figma: https://figma.redwood/example-eval-timeline (placeholder link).

2026-03-03 - Security review: we need approval for storing prompt samples that may contain PII. Prelim action: scrub samples with existing PII filter and flag evals marked 'sensitive' to opt out. Security review requested.

2026-03-06 - Routing policy discussion: allow teams to map thresholds to channels (e.g., team-x Slack for medium, PagerDuty for high); provide default templates. Add support for grouping by root cause (same commit/PR) to dedupe alerts.

2026-03-09 - Tradeoff: synchronous immediate reruns vs queued reruns. Decision: use a fast queued rerun for the first 30 seconds for low-cost sample, and schedule full rerun (longer) as background job. This balances latency vs cost.

2026-03-11 - QA plan: unit tests for grouping logic, e2e to simulate a model bump that triggers 3 eval regressions and ensure only one PagerDuty incident created when root cause is shared. Dashboard smoke tests for Console timeline.
